fixes.explanation: Yes, friend! The text says, "…no razor shall touch his head." (Numbers 6:5). He "…must let the hair of his head grow long." That razor is going to sit in the drawer feeling real left out.

Yes, friend! If someone suddenly dies in his presence and defiles his consecrated hair, "…he must shave his head on the day of his cleansing…" (Numbers 6:9). That's the seventh day. All that growing, and the hair has to come off anyway. I think that one hurts.

Oil is a nice thought, but this passage doesn't mention it for this moment. The text says he "…must shave his head on the day of his cleansing…" (Numbers 6:9). That's the seventh day. The consecrating of his head again comes later, after the offerings are made (Numbers 6:11). So the hair comes off first.

Seventh it is, baker! The text puts the day of his cleansing on the seventh day (Numbers 6:9). The very next day, the eighth, he brings two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 6:10). Good counting.
Third is a solid guess, but it's not the day the text gives. The day of cleansing is the seventh day (Numbers 6:9). The birds come on the eighth day (Numbers 6:10). Day three doesn't get a mention.

Tenth is a little past it, friend. The text says the day of cleansing is the seventh day (Numbers 6:9). The eighth day is when he brings two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest (Numbers 6:10). So the tenth day comes after both of those.

Nice hope, but it doesn't go that way. The text says, "But the preceding days shall not be counted, because his separation was defiled." (Numbers 6:12). He must rededicate his time of separation to the LORD. The days before don't carry over, so the count starts again.

The basket is in this passage, so I see the pull! But it holds "…unleavened cakes made from fine flour mixed with oil…" (Numbers 6:15). The hair goes "…on the fire under the peace offering." (Numbers 6:18). The text sends it to the fire, not the basket.

Yes, the priest! The priest waves the shoulder, the cake and the wafer before the LORD, and the text says, "This is a holy portion for the priest…" (Numbers 6:20). The text adds that it's in addition to the breast of the wave offering and the thigh that was presented. Good reading, baker.

True, baker! The text says, "After that, the Nazirite may drink wine." (Numbers 6:20). That comes after the shave and the wave offering. The time of separation is complete (Numbers 6:13). Patience paid off, friend.

Tempting when the days get long, I know! But the text says, "he must fulfill whatever vow he makes, according to the law of his separation." (Numbers 6:21). It doesn't mention shortening it. The word it uses is fulfill, so the vow is his to carry through.
